reviews.reason: The flagged .find probes one newly derived field-specific selector list once. The enclosing field list is exactly items/output for iteration or output for loop (at most two), and each call receives a different bindings field key because visibility differs between pre-body input and body output. A shared index would conflate those scopes; building a Map separately for a single lookup still scans every option and allocates an extra index. The current first matching selector preserves producer order and type semantics. Repeated variable-declaration lookup later in this validator has instead been indexed with first-match preservation. Container authoring and Workflow boundary tests assert immediate-body export, nested non-leakage and scalar input rejection.

The membership arrays at issue are fixed language/domain enums: exactly string/number/boolean/object/array for loop value types, and fail/break/continue for error policy. Neither collection grows with variables or graph size, so each includes check has a fixed bound of five or three comparisons and allocates no per-variable Set. Variable-name uniqueness already uses Set, and the repeated declaration lookup now uses a first-entry Map. Container contract declarations, typed editor options and authoring validation tests bind these exact field/type/error semantics; this review does not cover unbounded array membership.
